💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A GREAT UNDERSHIRT is my first line of defense against sweat, stains, and overheating.
  • Sources indicate that to find the GOATs, our fashion team and I tested more than 50 styles—everything from V-neck tees and tank tops to classic white crewnecks—wearing them under button-downs, sweaters, and even on their own.
  • Hanes is perhaps the most famous undershirt brand on the planet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A GREAT UNDERSHIRT is my first line of defense against sweat, stains, and overheating. It’s like the menswear equivalent of SPF. I learned that the hard way years ago, when I wore a flimsy cotton tee under a light-blue dress shirt to a summer wedding and, by cocktail hour, looked like I’d run a 10K instead of walked down the aisle. Never again. Now, if I’m layering under a dress shirt or sweater, I want something that works hard without me ever thinking about it. The best undershirts are so comfortable, I forget they’re even on. Unlike cheap, bulky options that ride up, trap heat, or lose their shape after a few washes, the real standouts are lightweight, moisture-wicking, and cut with a trim fit that stays put without squeezing the life out of you. They also tuck away neatly into trousers and save your other shirts from pit stains.

Sources indicate that to find the GOATs, our fashion team and I tested more than 50 styles—everything from V-neck tees and tank tops to classic white crewnecks—wearing them under button-downs, sweaters, and even on their own. The winners disappear under your clothes like a good stunt double, regulate temperature like built-in AC, and keep you looking cool, calm, and collected from your morning commute to last call.

Hanes is perhaps the most famous undershirt brand on the planet. I’ve been wearing its undergarments since I was about 10 years old, and over the time, they've just become better in terms of fit and feel. For example, I’ve been wearing Hanes’ performance undershirt for four months, and it’s consistently comfortable, breathable, and snug in all the right places.

The shoulders sit perfectly without pulling, the chest drapes close without clinging, and the sleeves are tailored to follow your arms without cutting into your biceps. When an undershirt feels this light, I brace myself for it to be flimsy and tear like tissue, but it's impressively solid—and I didn’t even sweat in it. Unlike other undershirts that I’ve tested, this one has a structured collar and hem that keeps its shape. The polyester-rayon fabric is extra smooth and cool to the touch, even after wearing it for hours at the office. I also appreciate that the fabric blend is much lighter in weight than a traditional cotton undershirt.

Sources indicate that after putting it through at least eight washes, I noticed that the fabric didn’t fade or shrink. One way I preserve it is by letting it air dry instead of tossing it in the dryer under high heat. It’s long enough to tuck in and doesn’t bunch under an overshirt. Since it's blended with a hint of stretch, I could grab a box off a high shelf without any restriction. Hanes uses the same double-needle stitching to reinforce the neck, sleeves, and hem as with their regular undershirts. This will stand up to years of washing and wearing with steady use. It only comes in white, but you can wear it with so many different fits—solo or layered.

Read More: Best T-Shirts for Men.

Mack Weldon was founded to reinvent men's underwear and loungewear with better fabric blends and quality construction. Take its V-neck style undershirt that I've been wearing for a couple months now. It’s cut from a polyamide-elastane blend—the same kind of technical fabric in our favorite workout clothes. It’s got that silky-soft hand feel with real stretch baked in. I can lift my arms, reach overhead, and wrestle into a jacket on the subway, and I don’t feel any tugging in the arms. The neckline sits low enough to disappear when I don’t want it to be seen under my dress shirts, but not so deep it feels flimsy or overly delicate.

What really sold me, though, is the breathability. Even under my chunky sweaters with some heft, I never break a sweat or find myself needing to flap my knit like I'm trying to cool off. Since it has a slim fit, it sits close to my skin without being tight, but stays dry when I’m making my way through the muggy subway or sitting in non-air-conditioned areas at the office. I tossed it in the wash at least six times and the white still looks just as good as the day it came out the pack.

Tommy John V-neck undershirt is step above your average option when it comes to polished layering. Its slim cut and modal fabric give it shape and structure, so it skims the body without feeling tight—perfect for showing off a chest workout without clinging in an unflattering way.

One of the best features is how it tucks. The snug-but-not-tight fit keeps the shirt neatly in place under dress shirts or sweaters, so you don’t get bunching or riding up. This makes it ideal for formal and office-ready attire, where a clean, smooth base layer is essential. It’s also stretchy without being too thin and has yet to pill, five washes later. I recommend letting it air dry, so it doesn’t shrink or become tight since the undershirt has a slim fit.

In a recent development, after multiple wears, the V collar doesn’t give “bacon neck”, which makes it look worn-out. It sits closer to the neck than Mack Weldon’s version, but I still can hide it by closing the top two buttons of my dress shirt. I love the buttery-soft feel, which is breathable and light even in warmer 70-degree temps.

Industry observers note that A major qualm with undershirts is their neckline can easily get ratted through the wash. We found Jockey's Made in America tees to keep a strong neckline and provide overall durability as an everyday undershirt. This is one of those cases where it's worth paying the extra bucks for an American-made garment.

Industry observers note that the Made in America factor isn't just for show. The quality that comes with it is apparent. The construction is clean and the fabric is thick enough that this undershirt can double as a plain white tee. So if you ever need to shed a layer or two, you can fall back on this as a base layer t-shirt. You can even style it on a hot day with just a pair of shorts.

More importantly, we found that Jockey has nailed the standard 100% cotton plain white undershirt in the best way possible. It feels like a traditional soft cotton tee, but after putting it through the wash and dry cycles more than a dozen times, it managed to withstand all the wear and tear and stay intact, proving its durability. The fabric even has a tech built-in to reduce piling and fading. And I love that the cotton is engineered to be able to wick away sweat in a heartbeat to keep me fresh all day. The only thing is that the fabric isn't wrinkle-resistant, so store these shirts carefully.

In a recent development, ATEK’s Stay Cooling undershirt is engineered for guys who run hot. The nylon-spandex blend feels slick and technical—almost like performance base-layer gear—but that’s exactly why it works. It wicks sweat fast, dries rapidly, and stays smooth under slimmer dress shirts without bunching or clinging. I’ve been wearing it while commuting and traveling since 2021, especially on days when I’m bouncing between the subway, the office, and post-work aims. The stretch makes it easy to move in, and after dozens of washes, it hasn’t shrunk or warped.

Recent findings suggest that gollayan put it through even tougher paces. He wore it under tailored dress shirts during long shoot days and under knit polos in the summer heat, noting that it kept sweat marks at bay and didn’t show through lightweight fabrics. He also flagged how well it holds its shape through the torso—no bacon-neck collar, no sagging by 4 p.m. If you love the soft, matte hand-feel of classic cotton, this one may feel a bit slick and synthetic. But that’s the trade-off for serious cooling power.

In a recent development, there has never been another brand with more hype around it than the early 1990s "My Calvins" undergarment campaign. But Calvin Klein's classic ribbed tank is not just hype, it is actually a really solid undershirt. If you prefer the minimal fabric feel of a tank or you just wear them when it's hot out then Calvins are hard to beat. And these, as undershirts, are practically perfect in terms of fabric, fit, and durability.

The full cotton fabric is stretchy despite having no built-in elastane or spandex. We love its soft-to-touch quality as well as natural breathability, the latter helps with wicking away sweat. The classic fit we found is slim without being constricting and they're just long enough to be tucked in if you need to but they can hang out without showing. The classic scoop neckline and seaming have also lasted well, and the fabric, even after over a dozen wash and dry cycles, has remained as stretchy, soft, and breezy.

For layering, we love putting it underneath a button-down or sweater/sweatshirt, though if you’re prone to underarm, we’d advise against this undershirt as your go-to.

Bugatchi’s crew neck tee is another great option that blurs the line between undershirt and standalone tee, but it leans more dressy than most. Made from a silky-soft Pima cotton, it has a luxe feel and fluid drape that’s more cocktail hour than couch rotting. I’ve worn it tucked into slacks with dress shoes for a fancy dinner, and it held its own. The fabric skims the body without clinging, and the finish reads sleek, not sporty.

It doesn’t have a durable ribbed collar like other dressier T-shirts, but it has a clean binding, which keeps its shape and frames the neck well. Compared to Reigning Champ’s athletic cut, this tee offers a touch more room in the torso, which flatters buffer guys. It layers neatly under jackets, but isn’t skin-tight. Out of all the undershirts on this list, this one has the best color options. When I'm heading into the city for dinner, I go with the mint to pair with cream dress pants for a clean, sharp ensemble. But for weekend errands or a coffee run, I throw on the air blue with jeans.

According to recent reports, gap has long been my go-to for affordable basics that punch above their price point. This undershirt is no different. While it’s not the trendiest or most technical, the shirt is made with an ultra-light, superfine jersey that’s buttery smooth, breathable, and almost weightless. It feels so nice and comfy that I lounge and sleep in it too. Unlike your average undershirt, which can feel a little thick or rough over time, this one stays silky and cool after multiple wears, making it perfect for layering under a blazer or shacket. Or, you could just throw it on to kick back on the couch.

According to recent reports, the straight fit is a major win for guys who want an undershirt that feels natural rather than overly snug or restrictive. The looser cut drapes smoothly over the body without awkward bunching, so you can wear it all day. In terms of the quality after washing, I have never seen the fabric pill. This kind of cotton manages to stay incredibly soft, cycle after cycle, speaking to its high quality.

At first glance, Reigning Champ’s jersey slim T-shirt might look like your everyday summer tee, but don’t be fooled. Yes, it has that easy, breezy fabric you want in a lightweight layer, but it’s not filmy, too thin, or see-through. It’s made from premium cotton that’s both smooth and breathable, yet structured enough that it retains its shape. I've tossed it in the wash at least four times now, and it still comes out looking good as latest. The cut is slim and subtly tapered at the hem, which looks sharp on athletic builds and lean frames.

Sources indicate that unlike looser, floppier collars that stretch out after a few cycles, this one is topped with a rib-bound collar that stays in place. It’s one of the only lightweight undershirts we tested where the collar didn’t droop, curl, or widen after wash two. I’ve worn it solo with shorts and jeans for coffee runs and quick errands. It also handled light activity in the park without showing any sweat and still looked fresh after hours of wear. Bonus: The color selection offers a number of neutrals that work for every outfit.

If you’re looking for the most breathable undershirt, it’s hard to beat the Uniqlo AIRism T-shirt. It’s made from a lightweight, high-tech fabric that consists of a polyester-elastane blend that dries rapidly and helps regulate body temperature to keep you cool and comfy all day. I wore the tee during a full-day shoot under a denim overshirt and didn’t overheat once even under direct sun and studio lights.

It has been revealed that it wicked away sweat faster than I expected and, more impressively, dried completely by the time I was back indoors. I also put it through a few airport and train travel days and the stretch fit held its shape, didn’t smell funky, and kept me feeling way fresher than any basic cotton tee could. Whether you’re layering it under a button-down or wearing it solo on a hot commute, it keeps you cool, not clammy, even in peak humidity.

Industry observers note that the ribbed texture is what really sets this tee apart from your average undershirt. It adds natural stretch and recovery, which means the shirt contours to your body, especially around the chest, arms and torso, without feeling tight or restrictive. The result? A more sculpted, flattering fit that holds its shape throughout the day. I tested it on a few hours-long photoshoots and can confirm: it doesn’t ride up, it breathes well, and the collar doesn’t sag by mid-afternoon.

Sources indicate that the fabric itself, a soft organic and recycled cotton-blend jersey, has just the right amount of weight. The fine ribbing, which creates raised vertical lines that look like subtle ridges, adds structure without veering into ’90s tank top territory, and the slim fit gives it that clean, tailored base layer vibe. It’s also a subtle style flex: If you shed your overshirt, this undershirt doesn’t look like a throwaway white tee. It actually holds its own, especially when paired with jeans or trousers.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a classic cotton undershirt that feels premium but not flashy, Brooks Brothers’ Supima Cotton V-Neck is it. It’s not built for performance like Mack Weldon’s tech-forward v-neck; it leans hard into comfort and breathability. Produced from Supima cotton, it’s noticeably smoother, softer, and more durable than other cotton shirts. It doesn’t hug the body as tightly, which actually makes it more forgiving on paunchier guts and more comfortable for long days on the move. This is the undershirt for guys who want something that disappears under button-ups; more work meeting than gym locker room.

I tested it under a white oxford shirt for a photoshoot at the office. The v-neck stayed completely hidden, even with the top two buttons undone, and the fit was trim enough that it didn’t bunch or add bulk under the shirt. Even under hot studio lights, I didn’t feel like I was sweating bullets. After three washes at home (cold wash, low tumble dry), the softness held up. It stayed smooth against the skin, with no pilling, collar warping or shrinkage. The seams stayed flat and clean, and the fabric has just enough weight to feel substantial, but still light enough to hide under thinner shirting.

Sources indicate that of all the undershirts we’ve tested, Fruit of the Loom’s 8-Pack easily provides the most value per wear. While it’s not as soft or moisture-wicking as more expensive shirts we’ve tried, it has a polyester-cotton blend that’s still comfortable and breathable enough to get you through the day. It doesn’t feel plastic-y, like other budget shirts we’ve tried. Rather, they have a natural cotton feel. Plus, the polyester blend does a competent job of wicking away sweat and helps keep its shape.

The Skims Classic T-shirt is a jack of all trades because it works as a base layer, a solo tee, or even a sleep shirt—it’s that comfortable. It offers stretch, meaning it moves with you, whether you’re lounging at home, running errands, or layering it under a jacket. This kind of flexibility makes it far more versatile than a standard undershirt, which can sometimes feel stiff or lose its shape over time.

The fabric is also lightweight and super breathable, so you won’t sweat if you decide to catch some Z’s in it. Unlike oversized loungewear tees or super tight compression shirts, this one sits in the middle ground with its classic fit and crew neck. It’s tailored enough to look clean under a cardigan but still relaxed to wear with joggers or jeans for an easy off-duty look.

It has been revealed that the key to the 72-Hour Tee is its merino wool fabric. Huckberry engineered this tee to utilize the natural features of merino wool, which is breathable, moisture-wicking, odor-resistant, and temperature-regulating. The goal of the 72-Hour Tee was to create an undershirt that you can wear for three days straight without getting gross. Our testers wore it during long flights as long as 16 hours overseas. While we initially didn’t like the neckline or the hem—we did find that the 72-Hour Tee managed to stay hidden in our outer garments. And with its merino build, the fabric passed our tests of smell, sweat, cooling, and softness even after hours of non-stop wear. We also found that the fabric is soft and doesn’t itch, and could withstand wash cycles like a pro.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes you need an extra thick base layer to build your outfit on top of. Enter the Field-Spec Cotton Heavy Tee from Buck Mason. It's made from a 100% cotton jersey fabric that was inspired by old rugby jerseys, which is twice as thick as the fabric of regular T-shirts.

It's the perfect undershirt for cold days or a plain T-shirt for rugged pursuits. It's cut in a classic fit that is slightly boxy but the sleeves are not too long. This is a heartier undershirt for those times when a light cotton or blend won't do, but you don't want to wear it for athletic activities or in extreme cold. That thick cotton will just absorb all your sweat and weigh you down if you're working out and put you at risk in the extreme cold.

The classic choice. Soft, breathable, and great for everyday wear. Look for Pima or Supima cotton—they’ve got longer fibers which means they’re softer, smoother, and way more durable than your run-of-the-mill cotton. The longer the fiber, the less fraying and pilling, so your tee stays looking fresh for way longer. That said, if you’re going 100% cotton, just know that while it’s still super breathable, it won’t dry as fast as those high-tech synthetic fabrics.

If you're an active guy, your undershirt material should also have a level of stretch (typically 5% or less)—courtesy of elastane or spandex—to help with flexibility and maintaining shape. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kia opened orders for two fresh PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK.
  • Sources indicate that the PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business.
  • So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia opened orders for two fresh PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK.

Sources indicate that the PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business. Built on Hyundai Motor’s dedicated modular skateboard platform, E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to enable “limitless possibilities.”.

So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.

Industry observers note that kia added the PV5 Chassis, an open-bed model that can be converted into just about anything. In the UK, Kia is offering conversions through TGS Automotive Group, including lightweight tipper, Dropside, and Box solutions.

The PV5 Chassis is available exclusively with the long-range 71.2 kWh battery in the UK, which Kia remarked could offer a potential WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km).

For reference, the PV5 Cargo L2/H1, which uses the same 71.2 kWh battery, offers a WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km). Other markets will also have a standard-range 51.1 kWh option.

The Chassis model is 4,610 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,935 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

Its compact size and 5.5-meter turning radius, Kia stated, make it easy to maneuver in city streets, construction sites, and other tight work areas.

In a recent development, inside, the PV5 Chassis features two seats. Like other variants, it includes a 12.9″ navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display with standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

According to recent reports, the Chassis model supports DC fast charging up to 120 kW, enabling the battery to charge from 10% to 80% in about 30 minutes. Using an 11 kW AC supply, it takes about 6 hours and 30 minutes to charge from 10% to 100%.

Payload depends on the configuration. Kia mentioned the Dropside offers a payload of up to 633 kg, while the Tipper can carry 561 kg.

In the UK, the PV5 Chassis is now on sale from £32,916 ($43,400) on the road, including the expected £5,000 ($6,700) UK Zero Emission Van Grant.

However, it’s an “incomplete vehicle,” as Kia describes it. The converted PV5 Dropside is priced from £40,110 ($53,500) on the road, including the ZEVG, while the PV5 Tipper starts at £41,310 ($55,000).

Kia also debuted the larger PV5 Cargo L2/H2 in the UK. The upcoming variant is 4,695mm long, 1,895mm wide, and 2,200mm high, with a 2,995mm wheelbase.

It has been revealed that the taller roof opens up an internal cargo-area height of 1,815mm. It also offers a greater load capacity than the L1/H1 and L2/H2, with 5.2 cubic meters.

It’s available in three- and four-door configurations with the choice of two or three seats. The three-door versions have a maximum payload of 630 kg, while the four-door models have dual sliding doors and offer a payload of up to 600 kg. Both versions can tow up to 1,500 kg.

Like the Chassis model, the PV5 Cargo L2/H2 is available in the UK exclusively with the 71.2 kWh battery, which provides a WLTP range of up to 239 miles.

Inside, it features the same setup as the other PV5 variants, including a 12.9″ touchscreen navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display.

The base PV5 Cargo L2/H2 Essential two-seat starts at £35,016 ($46,700), on the road, including ZEVG.

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After nearly 10 years in business, fashion designer Danielle Frankel Hirsch has opened a 12,000-square-foot location in Tribeca with interiors set to change the bridal game.
  • The nearly two-year design process is complete, and the Danielle Frankel bridal salon is now ready for appointments.
  • Frankel Hirsch on the staircase wearing a shirt she designed from Fortuny fabric.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After nearly 10 years in business, fashion designer Danielle Frankel Hirsch has opened a 12,000-square-foot location in Tribeca with interiors set to change the bridal game. To create the upcoming space, which opened in early November, Frankel Hirsch worked with AD PRO Directory designer Augusta Hoffman and Studio Partners Architecture.

The nearly two-year design process is complete, and the Danielle Frankel bridal salon is now ready for appointments. “We’re finally at the point where my heart and my head have been,” states Frankel Hirsch, who worked with Hoffman on her previous Los Angeles boutique and Latest York City atelier. “Because this is our third space together, we can almost speak in shorthand now.”.

Frankel Hirsch on the staircase wearing a shirt she designed from Fortuny fabric. Hoffman used the same Fortuny print throughout the space for wrapping side tables, keepsake boxes on the shelves, as well as for the woven seats on barstools.

The unassuming entrance to Danielle Frankel on Hudson Street.

In the reception room just inside the street entrance, the desk is custom, the chairs are antique, and the custom pendant is by Jamb.

Hoffman worked with the artist Miriam Ellner to create eglomise paneling surrounding the staircase. “The eglomise is one of my favorite things because when we were working with the artist we worked so intimately with her,” Frankel Hirsch indicates. “We worked on the placement the way that we do our laces. We kept going back and forth with the drawings because I wanted it to feel like our lace placement.”.

Recent findings suggest that on a recent morning, a bride and her wedding party were busy in the VIP suite making a final selection. The beaming group entered the space through an unassuming brown storefront entrance on Harrison Street, its two large glass windows encased in a sheer linen. From there they ascended a staircase up to a large gallery with over 30-foot floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the streets below on two sides, and a hand-painted mural pattern above on the ceiling.

The interiors of the original 19th-century Queen Anne–style red brick building were transformed by Hoffman (full disclosure: I am writing Hoffman’s design monograph publishing with Rizzoli in Fall 2027) into a modern, elegant bridal boutique that honors the history of the original Newly introduced York Mercantile Exchange, first established in the 1880s to keep the standards of the grocer business. “We wanted the space to stay pretty bright and focus on the architecture, but we needed a lot of seating,” Hoffman notes. “There was a lot of pressure because we wanted it to feel like Danielle and we wanted to leave our mark on the space, but it’s also so beautiful as is and we didn’t want to have too many interventions that take away from that.”.

Sources indicate that the rug, vintage Dutch leather armchairs, and custom clothing racks create one of the four seated zones in the gallery area. The wall features antique mottled glass windows. “We wanted this wall to feel historically accurate,” Hoffman notes.

Sources indicate that the custom oak screen features shelves for displaying miniature gowns by Danielle Frankel. The shelves are lined in silver leaf. The antique stool is reupholstered in a Fortuny fabric.

The view of the gallery area from a second floor bridal suite. The vintage teak seating set is reupholstered in a fabric by Manuel Canovas and the glass cocktail tables and Fortuny wrapped side tables are custom. The custom window panels are by Augusta Hoffman Studio for Wovn Home and the custom curtain hardware are bronze leaves designed by Hoffman. Hoffman pulled the leaf design from the details on the columns.

What previously functioned as a large, open space with a small mezzanine, had little existing infrastructure–no electrical, HVAC, or plumbing—and is now an area where brides can plot as they make the most important decision for their wedding day. In the gallery, Hoffman created distinct zones where wedding parties wait before their appointment in a private fitting room.

Recent findings suggest that much of the furniture was sourced by Hoffman and Frankel Hirsch together on trips to Paris. Antique glass vitrines separate the space, which they included from the previous Fresh York gallery and filled with Frankel Hirsch’s own family wedding photos as well as printed details brides can use for their fitting. One vitrine has a board layered with references of crinoline and interlining. Another has custom Danielle Frankel cufflinks. An oak folding screen lines one half of the room, with miniature gowns set on shelves lined in silver leaf paper. Custom parchment and cerused oak racks Hoffman designed to withstand the weight of a wedding dress line the floor displaying roughly 65 dresses from Danielle Frankel collections.

Industry observers note that the reflection of the wall is seen in the mirrored structure designed to house the elevator bank and stairwell to the street entrance. A framed antique floral plaster relief is flanked with 1930s Italian wall sconces in patinated glass and metal.

The staircase and elevator bank within the mirrored structure. “We had to add the elevator for function and for code, and we were like ‘How do we take this existing architecture and put an elevator in the middle of the room?’” Hoffman says. “It feels super unexpected, versus trying to hide it, and you get to see more of the surrounding architecture and light in the reflection.”.

The custom rug is topped with an antique stool upholstered in a Fortuny fabric, a 1950s chair, and a 19th-century English pine console table.

Industry observers note that the view from the sitting area adjacent to a bar. The vintage teak seating set was among the first items Hoffman and Frankel Hirsch sourced for the space. The custom bar stool is woven with a Fortuny fabric.

The view from within the staircase to the gallery area. The custom center table is by Rafael Carneiro Triboli and the French chairs are from the 1930s.

Hoffman and Studio Partners Architects took what was formerly the mezzanine, originally separated from the below with only a single-bar metal railing, and made it into a full wall with antiqued mottled glass windows. In the center they constructed a cascading grand staircase, cleverly concealing the stockroom underneath, which leads upstairs to three private bridal suites. The hallways, painted in Wenge by Benjamin Moore, lead to the bridal suites, each designed differently and filled with antique and vintage furniture, custom carpets, lighting, and racks. The walls are painted in Presidente Roman Clay by Portola Paints, an earthy contrast to the white and ivory dresses, which are naturally the center of attention for visitors in each room.

Industry observers note that when guests are finished in their suites, there’s a bar in the gallery space where wedding parties can sit and make the final selection. The wedding party that morning had selected the dress and were toasting champagne to celebrate. “It’s just as much about the hospitality and the warmth as it is about the gowns,” Frankel Hirsch says.

In a recent development, in the VIP bridal suite, which can be accessed through a discreet entrance on Harrison Street, the custom sofa is upholstered in Holland & Sherry’s Corbel in Henna. The artwork features fragments of 19th century Japanese brocade.

The midcentury armchairs are upholstered in a Watts 1874 fabric and flank a vintage oak table.

The rack, mirror, and ceiling pendant are all custom in the VIP bridal suite.

In the dressing area of the VIP bridal suite, the ceiling pendant is custom and the closet wall covering is by Watts 1874.

The 1930s lounge chair is reupholstered in a Fortuny fabric and the 1970s lamp is from Brazil.

Tesla tuner Unplugged offers to take over Cybertruck production

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive.
  • It comes just four days after Elon Musk stated Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.
  • UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The firm notes it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive. The company publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors.

It comes just four days after Elon Musk stated Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.

UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The firm notes it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”.

In exchange, Tesla would collect a license fee plus FSD and Robotaxi network revenue on every vehicle built. UP even offered to let Cybercab get first call on battery cells. “We’ll wait our turn,” the tech giant wrote.

UP founder Ben Schaffer made it clear that he supports Tesla’s all-in move to autonomy, but he wants to keep the Cybertruck program alive.

According to recent reports, and it isn’t stopping at the pickup. UP says it would build the Cybertruck, a three-row “CyberSUV,” and an unmanned “CyberCargo” hauler. Two vehicles Tesla has sometimes referenced, but they were never unveiled.

Industry observers note that the post passed 240,000 views within hours, and the replies are mostly Cybertruck owners and Tesla shareholders begging Musk to say yes. Neither Musk nor Tesla had publicly responded at the time of writing.

Recent findings suggest that UP has a lot riding on this. It sells an entire Cybertruck product line, the UP Invincible lift and armor kits, and it has scored several contracts to turn Cybertrucks into police vehicles for law enforcement agencies. CEO Ben Schaffer once described the organization’s purpose as doing “the things that Tesla maybe wants to do, but doesn’t have the bandwidth to do.” This is that idea taken to its extreme.

Musk framed the Cybertruck’s end as a space problem. He said Tesla needs to “make room for increased Cybercab production.”.

If the Cybertruck program was successful, Tesla wouldn’t be killing it. Tesla also produces Model Ys at Giga Texas, and it is not shutting that down to make room for Cybercab.

As we reported when Tesla revealed the wind-down, that explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of floor space, the Cybertruck line runs at about a quarter of its 125,000-unit installed capacity, and Texas had only a few hundred Cybercabs registered as of late October.

The real problem is buyers. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3, and we estimated 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks, a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. That was a good quarter by Cybertruck standards.

It has been revealed that even that number flatters it. S&P Global Mobility data showed SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, about 18% of US registrations that quarter. Tesla also tried a cheaper RWD trim, killed it, launched a $60,000 AWD version, then raised prices by $5,000 in August. None of it fixed demand.

According to recent reports, I’ll give UP credit for this: the offer calls Musk’s bluff. If the Cybertruck is really dying because Cybercab needs the room, here’s someone volunteering to take the line off Tesla’s plate. Problem solved.

Of course, it’s more complicated than that.

There are many ways this could fail or never happen in the first place, but there’s also a slight possibility that makes this possible.

First off, the backlash is real. If you look on social media and forums, yes, most of the discussion is about how Cybertruck is a failure, and Elon is lying about why Tesla is killing it, but there’s also a serious group of people, especially Cybertruck owners, who are genuinely upset that Tesla is killing the program because they love their trucks.

Most people have never driven a Cybertruck, but the steer-by-wire makes it a very addictive vehicle to drive, and even though the price is high, the value proposition for the specs is not bad compared to the very limited options for electric pickup trucks.

In other words, I wouldn’t necessarily bet against this effort, especially if they add an SUV variant and show the program some love with some tweaks here and there.

I could see a group of wealthy Cybertruck fans pooling money under Unplugged to make this happen, but getting Tesla to agree could be hard. It’s not unheard of for an automaker to sell a vehicle program to a dealer, like the Lotus Seven and Studebaker Avanti, but it would be a first at this scale.

#52660. Latest Update: It’s that time again – Honda needs to roll out an electric Super Cub

Latest Update: It’s that time again – Honda needs to roll out an electric Super Cub

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already.
  • I’m not talking about an electric scooter vaguely inspired by the Super Cub.
  • The Honda Super Cub is arguably the most successful motor vehicle ever created, with well over 100 million produced since its introduction in 1958.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already.

I’m not talking about an electric scooter vaguely inspired by the Super Cub. Not another futuristic concept with swoopy bodywork and a name that looks like a Wi-Fi password. I mean an actual honest-to-goodness Honda Super Cub, except electric.

The formula is already sitting right there.

The Honda Super Cub is arguably the most successful motor vehicle ever created, with well over 100 million produced since its introduction in 1958. It’s still in continuous production today.

It has been revealed that and a huge part of that success comes down to how approachable the thing is. It isn’t supposed to be intimidating, excessively powerful, or particularly complicated. It’s simple, practical transportation wrapped in one of the most recognizable two-wheeler designs ever created.

In other words, it’s practically begging to become electric.

Sources indicate that the beauty of the bike is how simple and timeless it is, with the appearance barely changing in nearly 7 decades. And with the design freedom that electric drivetrains provide, upgrading the cute little bike to an electric future would be a walk in the park for Honda’s engineers.

An in-wheel motor would be a simple, cheap solution that frees up even more space in the body for batteries.

Recent findings suggest that and Honda wouldn’t need some enormous battery capable of highway touring. Give an electric Super Cub enough battery for perhaps 50-60 miles (80-95 km) of real-world urban riding, a motor capable of roughly 50-60 mph (80-95 km/h), and simple Level 1 charging from a normal wall outlet. As a city runabout or a beachside cruiser, those middle-of-the-road specs would be perfect.

According to recent reports, even better, make the battery removable. Honda already has its Mobile Power Pack e: swappable battery system used in various electric two-wheelers, and an electric Super Cub would be an incredible platform to expand it.

The resulting bike could hit an unusually sweet spot.

It has been revealed that there are millions of people riding electric bicycles today who will eventually want something faster, but don’t necessarily want a 500-pound (220 kg) electric motorcycle capable of hitting 120 mph (200 km/h). An electric Super Cub would be a natural next step: light, unintimidating, easy to ride, cheap to operate, and fast enough to actually function as a real urban vehicle.

It would also be one of the rare electric motorcycles that could appeal to people who aren’t necessarily looking for an “electric motorcycle.” An electric version is in such high demand that companies specialize in retrofit kits to convert classic Cubs into EVs.

According to recent reports, the Super Cub already has decades of cultural cachet. It’s cute. It’s useful. It’s nostalgic without feeling ancient. It’s the kind of motorcycle that can appeal equally to a lifelong rider and someone who has never considered owning a motorcycle before.

Sources indicate that and perhaps most importantly, Honda could actually sell the thing globally. The same basic electric Super Cub could work in dense European cities, throughout Asia, and in American cities and suburbs. It doesn’t need to win spec-sheet battles. It just needs to be affordable, reliable, and unmistakably a Super Cub.

It has been revealed that my mum's old Honda-50 (the original cub, early 70's) had a tank that held less than a gallon of petrol. Range was realistically about 50 miles, but no-one even thought about that, it never ran out.

She traded for a honda-90, then a bunch of other stuff, I miss that 90, even now.

But the point is that range is not the issue, very few trips on these are more than 10 - 15 miles, say 30km round-trip.

But the real range, on a battery vehicle, is only about 2/3 of the claim,.

so if the claim is 80, it'll maybe do 55?

Thats enough, if it has the zip to handle traffic, and cruise at 45 - 50mph.

According to recent reports, honda has already shown that it understands the importance of electrifying small two-wheelers. It’s even made a token gesture with a Cub-like e-scooter in China. But there’s a difference between making another electric scooter and electrifying perhaps the most famous small motorcycle ever made.

So here I am once again, Honda.

Sources indicate that you’ve got the name. You’ve got the design. You’ve got the batteries. You’ve got the manufacturing scale.

Just put all the pieces together and give us the electric Super Cub already. The world is waiting, and will thank you.

#52658. Latest Update: Fera Fruit Oil Claims It’s Healthier Than Even Avocado Oil. Should You Make the Switch?

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1086 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Menshealth ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Fera Fruit Oil Claims It’s Healthier Than Even Avocado Oil. Should You Make the Switch?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1086 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EREWHON, EVERYONE’S FAVORITE love-to-hate overpriced supermarket chain made news recently for switching up their oils.
  • In a recent development, erewhon isn’t the only company hawking fera fruit oil as a way to further health-ify their vegan buffalo cauliflower and turmeric chicken tenders.
  • Fera fruit oil may sound exotic and healthy (it’s made from fruit?), but as a registered dietitian, I'm not one for assumptions when it comes to food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EREWHON, EVERYONE’S FAVORITE love-to-hate overpriced supermarket chain made news recently for switching up their oils. Yes, the certified organic grocer unveiled that it's no longer using avocado oil to fry its cafe food. Instead, all 15 locations are switching to certified organic fera fruit oil.

In a recent development, erewhon isn’t the only company hawking fera fruit oil as a way to further health-ify their vegan buffalo cauliflower and turmeric chicken tenders. Since launching in April 2026, the oil is now in more than 800 grocers, restaurants, wellness clubs, and luxury hotels like Mezeh Mediterranean Grill and Wynn Las Vegas.

Fera fruit oil may sound exotic and healthy (it’s made from fruit?), but as a registered dietitian, I'm not one for assumptions when it comes to food. Especially when it coincides with the peak of seed-oil fear-messaging. Keep reading to learn what this upcoming-to-the-scene frying oil is and if it's really worth the hype.

Industry observers note that FERA FRUIT OIL is basically palm oil. The company behind it, Zero Acre Farms, trademarked the name “fera fruit oil” for high oleic palm oil, a type of palm oil that's produced by pressing the fruit of a hybrid palm tree called Oleifera × Guineensis (OxG for short).

Industry observers note that the hybrid plant was originally planted by farmers to reduce bud rot, a disease that notoriously destroys palm crops. A happy side effect was that the oil also ended up having higher oleic acid content, the same heart-healthy monounsaturated fat found in avocado and olive oil.

TRADITIONALLY GROWN PALM has a problematic history of deforestation, but according to Zero Acre Farms, fera fruit oil is a perennial crop that requires just 0.3 acres to produce a ton of oil, using 15 to 20 times less land than soybean or canola oil.

It has been revealed that of course, Zero Acre Farms’ website doesn't cite sources for these numbers, so I did my own digging. Independent research suggests traditional palm yields 3.3 tons per hectare, which is impressive compared to soybean, canola, and sunflower, which collectively produce 0.6 tons per hectare. But OxG palm yields about 1 ton less than traditional palm, which means the demonized seed oils use 3 to 4 times more land, not 15 to 20 times. So the claims seem a bit sensationalized at best?

COMPARED WITH REGULAR palm oil, high oleic palm oil—including the trademarked fera fruit oil—offers a significant nutritional upgrade.

In a recent development, traditional palm oil contains about 50 percent saturated fat, including about 40 percent oleic acid, and 10 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids. OxG, the hybrid that produces fera fruit, contains 50 percent oleic acid, 33 percent saturated fatty acids, and 12 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids.

As a dietitian, I can get behind these improvements, but the benefits don't translate to real-world benefits quite as well.

The only way you'll eat fera fruit oil is if you're enjoying pre-made food, most likely fried food, from an establishment using it, as it's not right now available for consumer purchase. And while food fried in fera fruit oil may be slightly nutritionally better than traditional palm oil (which most establishments in the U.S. aren't using anyway), it's still fried food.

Industry observers note that this ratio not only contains less saturated fat, but also helps maintain stability over multiple rounds of deep frying compared to other oils. A study presented at the 21st International Oil Palm Conference found that high oleic palm oil lasted more rounds of frying than palm, sunflower, soy, or canola. Because it has less polyunsaturated fat and more monounsaturated and saturated fat, it resists degradation better. This adds up to cost savings, because the oil can be used multiple times, but there's unlikely much of a health advantage. Deep-frying meat and starchy foods in any oil can create harmful compounds, but the link between reusing oil, oil stability, and human health is less clear.

It has been revealed that unrefined high oleic palm oil is rich in antioxidants, including carotenoids and vitamin E. Fera fruit oil is marketed as clean, neutral-tasting, and expeller-pressed, but it offers no guarantee or information on what antioxidants are in the bottle at use or how much.

In a recent development, so while this all sounds great on paper, it's hard to tell how it actually translates into real-world benefits. Is it worth the hype? I'd personally like to see tangible evidence that it does before shelling out extra money for it, and that evidence doesn't seem to exist yet.

Recent findings suggest that prior to October 15, Erewhon used avocado oil in its fryers. So while there's no arguing that Fera fruit oil has a healthier fatty acid profile than regular palm oil, how does it compare to other fruit oils, like avocado and olive oil, in terms of both health and sustainability?

Recent findings suggest that while olive oil has strong evidence supporting its positive effects on human health, especially heart health, clinical research on the health effects of high-oleic palm oil, like Fera fruit oil, is limited. In one study, 160 participants had either 25 mL of high oleic palm oil or 25 mL of extra virgin olive oil daily for three months. Both groups had similar reductions in total cholesterol and LDL-cholesterol. While these results are promising, the study was small, and more clinical trials are needed to confidently say high oleic palm oil is as beneficial as olive oil.

Avocado oil has a favorable fatty acid profile of 71 percent monounsaturated fatty acids, 13 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids, and 16 percent saturated fatty acids. Fera fruit oil has more saturated fat and less monounsaturated fat, but no head-to-head studies have tested their health effects.

When an elite grocery store like Erewhon switches to a fresh fryer oil, it's easy to assume it's the healthiest choice. But I wouldn't be so quick to jump on board.

After reviewing the research and understanding the food climate we're currently in, where seed oils are viewed as the culprit of all disease and beef tallow is a cure-all, this honestly seems like just another misguided trend. In the context of reality, when you eat an overall healthy and balanced diet, the occasional fried food, whether it's fried in avocado oil, canola oil, or fera fruit oil, will likely have very little impact on your overall health.

Kelsey Kunik, RDN, is a registered dietician and health writer who covers all-things nutrition for Men's Health and Women's Health.

#52655. ‘Dune: Part Three’: An Exclusive First Look at the Sets

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1093 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Architecturaldigest ↗ Open Full Page

‘Dune: Part Three’: An Exclusive First Look at the Sets

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1093 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nothing about the cinematic language of Dune is small—director Denis Villeneuve’s film trilogy does span multiple planets, after all.
  • Industry observers note that “My approach has always been with symbolism and semiotics,” Vermette tells AD.
  • In conversation with Vermette about the sci-fi epic, examples of that core tenet come up often.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nothing about the cinematic language of Dune is small—director Denis Villeneuve’s film trilogy does span multiple planets, after all. But throughout his work on the movies, including the upcoming Dune: Part Three, production designer Patrice Vermette has made sure to stay focused on the little details.

Industry observers note that “My approach has always been with symbolism and semiotics,” Vermette tells AD. “It is my philosophy of design, because for Denis, empty design cannot exist. Things need to have a purpose. Need to have a signification.”.

In conversation with Vermette about the sci-fi epic, examples of that core tenet come up often. Carefully designed details imbue hidden meaning in each set, creating a captivating, immersive on-screen world that earned the designer an Oscar for his work in the first Dune. The trilogy’s latest installment, Dune: Part Three, which lands in theaters on December 18, expands on that ethos. And for the final film in the series, the sheer scale of the sets was larger. “It was our last chance working in that world,” Vermette claims. “It’s like in a fireworks [display], it’s the end, it’s the bouquet final, it’s like, ‘alright, let’s do it!’”.

Robert Pattinson as Scytale, with director Denis Villeneuve.

Sources indicate that over 450,000 square feet of interior stages and 475,000 square feet of backlots were used for scenes shot in Budapest alone, with each set typically taking 14 to 16 weeks to build. (Filming also took place in Abu Dhabi and Iceland.) Even the sandworms that slither through the titular dunes got grander this time around: Instead of the relatively small platforms that were used to film worm-riding sequences as in the previous films, the production team built a 300-foot-long by 65-foot-wide sandworm in the middle of the desert.

Like in Dune: Part Two, Vermette was challenged to create entirely newly introduced sets for this installment, which adapts Frank Herbert’s 1969 novel Dune Messiah. One of the new settings viewers can expect is Wallach IX, the home of the powerful and secretive Bene Gesserit sisterhood. Throughout their planet, Vermette incorporated stone etchings that resemble human cells seen through a microscope, referencing the Bene Gesserit’s breeding program that has gone on for millennia. Mother nature also informed the architecture. “When you arrive on the planet, the buildings are basically eggs of a spider, like crops of spider eggs as you find them in nature,” Vermette explains. “Ecology has always been a huge source of inspiration for me, and also for the storytelling it gives—you know, they’ve got their web across the universe, for the genealogy they create.”.

It has been revealed that another fresh setting is the Veteran’s District, where the Fremen, the native inhabitants of the desert planet Arrakis, retire after fighting in the catastrophic holy war spurred by Paul Atreides, aka Muad’Dib (Timothée Chalamet). In the previous films, the Fremen lived in communal residences lined with hand-carved stone that recorded their history and culture. Returning from the battlefield, they find mass-produced housing units instead of the “green paradise” they were promised would await them. Made of ceramic instead of rock, with stamped-on rather than hand-carved markings, the Veteran’s District represents an artificial facsimile of their former homes. “And when you put all these units together, and you look at the rooftops, it’s there to represent sand dunes,” Vermette explains. “All these triangles align [to look like dunes], but it’s fake.”.

Another circular doorway represents an all-seeing eye near the lush Imperial Gardens, which illustrate Paul’s extreme wealth and control of resources—including water—on the dry planet of Arrakis.

There is a green paradise on Arrakis, just not for the Fremen. Lush gardens grace the planet’s Imperial Palace, a massive inverted pyramid with a large circle cut out of it—a reimagined version of the all-seeing eye. “I got inspired by the title of the book, Messiah, and from the fact that Denis, just like Frank Herbert, wanted to make sure that Paul Atreides was not going to be seen as a hero, and it’s a tale of being cautious about messianic figures,” says Vermette. Similar representations of the all-seeing eye are found throughout the palace, sinisterly implying that Muad’Dib is always watching.

In actuality, Muad’Dib’s personal quarters are completely isolated from the rest of the palace. His wife, Irulan (Florence Pugh), must find her way through a twisting mass of hallways to reach him. “Basically, she’s walking into the psyche of Paul,” Vermette explains. “She goes into a void, and then it’s all these mazes of one’s mind.” When we get to the end of the maze, we see that Paul’s inner sanctum resembles a humble desert camp. Not unlike the Fremen, his dwelling has been reduced to an echo of what once was. He is “living as a recluse because he doesn’t trust anybody,” Vermette explains. “He wants to go back to a place where he felt the most comfortable, which was the desert. So he recreated that space.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Denis really wanted that set to be the golden cage of Irulan,” Vermette indicates of these private chambers. “She’s married to the emperor, but she’s not free at all, she’s a prisoner.” The window is shaped similar to an infinity symbol, but is covered in metal screens. “It’s like eternity, but eternity is blocked. It’s like a cage.”.

The entrance to the maze within Muad’Dib’s inner sanctum. Vermette designed 40 maze wall panels that needed to be moved into various configurations to shoot the scene, which was filmed in less than a day. Eight people were each assigned a portion of the 12-foot-high panels and learned a choreography of sorts, rapidly moving into each configuration until they could do each one in five minutes or less. “We rehearsed and rehearsed, just like dancers or musicians; they knew exactly where to fit their pieces” within the roughly 14,400-square-foot space, says Vermette.

On the planet Wallach IX, the office of Bene Gesserit Reverend Mother Mohaim features stone carvings inspired by human cells under a microscope.

Recent findings suggest that the Imperial Palace throne room took 20 weeks to build. Behind Muad’Dib’s emerald throne, the windows are shielded with metal cast screens inspired by Montreal’s Saint-Ambrose Church, which was built in 1925 by architect Ernest Cormier.

The all-seeing eye is a repeating symbol Vermette inserted throughout the Imperial Palace, including a representation seen here as the circular entrance of Paul’s Keep.

The architecture of this Imperial Palace corridor has slanted walls to reflect a pyramid-shaped exterior and flying buttress support structures inspired by Gothic-style cathedrals.

6 Best Heart Rate Monitors, Tested by Our Fitness Editors

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • TRAINING WITHOUT TRACKING is like shooting a basketball without knowing where the hoop is, especially if you have an ultimate goal like running a marathon or increasing your VO2 max.
  • According to recent reports, A few of the most crucial insights are heart rate variability (HRV), which describes the difference in time between the beats of your heart, and resting heart rate (RHR), which is the number of times your heart pumps while you are awake, relaxed and not moving.
  • Industry observers note that understanding your HRV can help you make better workout choices and understand when it's time to recover.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TRAINING WITHOUT TRACKING is like shooting a basketball without knowing where the hoop is, especially if you have an ultimate goal like running a marathon or increasing your VO2 max. Many people reach a point in their fitness journey where they hit a plateau, and more often than not, that flatline results from not having the right information. So if you're hitting the gym on a regular basis and putting in the work, it can be key to make sure that you are getting all the relevant health insights to make sure you're using your time efficiently.

According to recent reports, A few of the most crucial insights are heart rate variability (HRV), which describes the difference in time between the beats of your heart, and resting heart rate (RHR), which is the number of times your heart pumps while you are awake, relaxed and not moving. Heart rate monitors (HRMs) are the best way to get this data.

Industry observers note that understanding your HRV can help you make better workout choices and understand when it's time to recover. Generally speaking, your resting heart rate will become lower as your fitness level increases, indicating more efficient heart function and improved cardiovascular fitness. “Over time (and months of tracking your resting heart rate), you'll notice patterns. Maybe your RHR spikes every weekend, in part because you're out late Saturday nights. Or it's lower on Mondays, because you go to bed earlier on Sundays," indicates MH Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. "All of this data can help you make smart lifestyle tweaks that aid your overall wellness — and set you up to move, look, and feel your best and most alert, whether you're in the gym or at the office.”.

Industry observers note that with the holidays coming up fast, it’s a good time to add a heart rate monitor to your wish list. It can help you start your New Year’s training goals on a data-driven note, and allow you to track your progress over time.

Recent findings suggest that ready to take your training to the next level? Read on to find the best heart rate monitors for you and what to consider when looking for a HRM.

Sources indicate that we've been raving about Whoop for years, and it's still one of our favorite fitness trackers simply because it collects so much useful data. This stylish and understated device uses PPG sensors to continuously check your heart rate, and can use the data it captures to figure out when your deepest sleep is happening.

According to recent reports, every day it delivers a recovery percentage and suggests the level of activity you should aim for, whether that a five-mile run or a rest day. In the past, the brand stuck with a simple black band, but these days there are more color and style options for anyone wanting to elevate the look of their HRM.

I personally am a fan of the ability to check my insights when I want, without a distractingly bright screen that pulls my attention.

In a recent development, while products like the Whoop band and the Oura Ring are relatively newly introduced on the scene, Garmin has been making wearable fitness trackers for a long time now. This heart rate monitor transmits real-time heart rate data over ANT+ connectivity and Bluetooth, giving you the immediate feedback you need to take your performance to the next level.

Industry observers note that this Garmin comes with a rechargeable battery with a seriously long life (two months). It charges easily using the provided 4-pin charging cable, similar to the ones that come with their watches.

According to recent reports, we were also impressed with how comfortable this strap is to wear, made out of a lightweight nylon weave. For placement, you want to put the sensor in the middle of your ribcage against your skin, not over your clothes, so that it can get the best readings. Once you are done with your run, you will be able to connect it to your smartphone or Garmin watch via Bluetooth, and then pull up your stats from the menu option.

Because this Garmin has Bluetooth, it is also able to connect pretty simply to cardio machines at your gym like treadmills if you want to track your workouts there. If you are a Garmin fan, and want even more functionality and access to the Garmin Connect app, you may want to spring for the Garmin HRM Pro model (about $60 more).

Read More: Best Fitness Trackers, Tested by Us.

According to recent reports, this is a subtle and sleek way to monitor your heart rate throughout the day. Most people aren't going to wear a ring like this while lifting weights, which is why we love the Oura Ring to track those notable metrics during the 23 hours of the day that you're not at the gym. What's most impressive about the Oura Ring is its small size, and how one small ring can monitor your sleep, steps, and heart rate.

In a recent development, this ring gives you all the information you need to make improvements in your daily health and well-being. For those looking to try a smart ring for the first time, it doesn't get better than Oura, which is why it took the top spot in our best smart rings testing and this head-to-head piece against the Samsung Galaxy Ring.

Industry observers note that read More: The Oura Ring Vs. the Galaxy Ring.

It has been revealed that the Apple Watch is by far one of the most popular smartwatches on the market, and like the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, it also tracks quite a lot of data, including heart rate. Although not as accurate as the chest bands, the Apple Watch 12 gets the job done well enough for the casual fitness goer.

In addition to heart rate, it also features an SpO2 sensor to monitor blood oxygen level readings, an ECG to test for atrial fibrillation, fitness tracking, sleep monitoring, and all the run-of-the-mill smartwatch features. Our editors have already spent some time with this latest release, and it's fair to say we're suitably impressed.

It has been revealed that the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 is essentially a wearable personal trainer and advisor powered by AI. With built-in pace coaching and a heart rate monitor, you can add and customize your workouts for maximum efficiency, helping you reach your fitness goals in no time. It connects to your smartphone so you can easily take calls, receive texts, or pull up directions with the flick of your wrist.

The newer design is certainly better looking than previous editions. The integrated Run Coach also impressed some of our editors, guiding those who require additional motivation.

That being remarked, despite the fact that the Galaxy Watch 8 supports iOS and iPhone people through its companion app, those users might be better over going for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for the additional integrations. The heart rate measurements and sleep tracking is where this device really shines, which is perfect for those looking for a new HRM.

Read more: Best Smartwatches, Tested By Us.

It has been revealed that while it’s not the latest version, the Pixel Watch 4 from Google is packed with useful features beginners will appreciate. (The Pixel Watch 5 is the newest iteration, but significantly more expensive.) One of our favorites is Active Zone Minutes, which uses your resting heart rate to gauge exercise effort and give you a buzz when it's time to step up the intensity so you can make the most of your workouts. It monitors activity, sleep, and nightly blood oxygen levels, tracking your trends over time to see key changes in your overall health.

This is a great pick for anyone looking to get great health insights from a wrist piece, who also would like a subtly stylish look. Since Google now owns Fitbit, this watch features some of that great Fitbit technology, which means there are a lot of great integrations if you have a Google account. But because of this, the pairing with iOS devices is not optimal. Something to take into consideration if you're an Apple user.

Google also knows how to make app experiences easy on upcoming users, including older users without a lot of time with technology.

The biggest determination you need to make before purchasing is what your primary goal is for the heart rate monitor. Competitive triathletes may want to splurge on a top-shelf device that wraps around your chest for the most accurate data. Whereas beginners or more casual consumers might opt for a more modest option they can wear throughout the day (like a general fitness tracker) for daily health insights. Perhaps you spend a lot of time on the golf course and want to know how your heart handles hours of walking combined with the stress of trying to make par. Of course, you may be one of those high-performing individuals who uses both.

Beyond finding a device that fits your performance needs, you also need one that fits well on your body. This depends on whether you choose a chest strap, a wristband, or a smart ring. In most cases, the sensors need to be secured tightly against your body to get accurate readings. Take accurate body measurements before ordering offline, and be prepared to return for a different size if you need to (especially with something like a chest strap). If you are looking into smart rings, many of the options, like the Oura Ring we list, will ship out sizing kits for a small fee to get the correct fit.

According to recent reports, great data is useless if you don’t have an easy means of getting it. For devices without screens, make sure you check which smartphones and apps they are compatible with. They will usually connect with your personal devices through Bluetooth. For devices with screens, check images of the user interface to make sure you’ll enjoy it. Of course, the devices we are suggesting here with screens will display all the crucial information you’ll want. But some may have better compatibility with iOS or Android, which you’ll want to consider.

Recent findings suggest that with the exception of the Apple Watches (Ultra 3 and Series 11) and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 (two heart rate monitors that are equal parts smartwatch), the heart rate monitors we tested are all designed to run for days (even weeks) on a single charge. We love a heart rate monitor that needs minimal charging, and we also love one that lasts a long time in non-connected mode. Two heart rate monitors that surprised us when testing battery life include the Garmin HRM-Dual (3.5 years if used for one hour a day) and the Oura Ring (7 days while on).

Recent findings suggest that being the Fitness and Commerce Editor at Men's Health, it's my job to evaluate the latest and greatest training gear. This includes fitness trackers, and throughout the year, I get the latest designs from the best brands, both upcoming and old. I am also a certified trainer, and my personal training includes a wide range of exercises, from boxing to lifting to sprint work. But this story was a collective effort by several editors, who were enlisted to try different models and types of trackers based on their preferences.

We tested each tracker for at least two weeks and put it through a range of exercise scenarios, from treadmill sprints to weighted pull-ups to deadlifts. My fellow testers included certified trainers who also happen to be editors at Men's Health, like Samuel. For devices that have been around for several updates, we've used most of them since they hit the market. Our tested selection didn't focus on chasing trends. Instead, our picks of the best fitness trackers provide great value and performance at reasonable price points for the data they provide.

All of these factors went into finding our favorite heart rate monitors.

Charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. Following an early life in athletics, Charles became a NASM-certified trainer and began writing programs alongside the most respected coaches in the world. Since entering the world of fitness content, Charles has had the opportunity to learn from and train alongside high performance individuals from the NFL, UFC, NBA, Formula 1, CrossFit, US Olympics, and Navy SEALs. When he’s not writing about training programs or gear, he can be seen at the gym or in the wild, putting them to the test.

  • Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.

This isn’t just a normal model release. For one, it’s incredibly good. Neon posts 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 59 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6.2 Sol. It takes the Vals Index at 70.9%, AutomationBench at 56.3% against Opus 5.5’s 42.5%, and GraphWalks long-context retrieval at 95.2% against Opus 5.5’s 66.8%.

In a recent development, beyond just the outperformance, Google has been releasing at a pace nobody else is matching. It dropped Argon in mid-October. Carbon on October 28. Hydrogen last week. Google owns its silicon, its data centers, and its distribution, and it is using all three to iterate faster than labs that rent compute. And it has some speculating that Google has already achieved RSI (recursive self-improvement), the final step ahead of super intelligence.

So Google has caught up at the top of the AI race. Just in time for the ANT IPO.

In a recent development, anthropic will be priced at $83, 6.4% above the top of its $70 to $78 range, valuing the company around $1.5 trillion fully diluted. On the 825 million shares in the original terms, that’s roughly $68.5 billion raised, and about $94.5 billion counting the separate $26 billion private placement from its compute suppliers. It trades Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Notably, ANT has been trading on Hyperliquid in the $90-$100 range for the past week but popped to $105 this morning.

Industry observers note that the valuation math is a 55% step-up from the $965 billion May round and about 25% below the $2 trillion Anthropic was reportedly chasing in September. Revenue ran $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier, a 13x increase. Annualize that and $1.5 trillion is roughly 34 times sales.

Industry observers note that that’s a steep raise given the macro backdrop and the Fed calling for more hikes for longer. AI stocks have been shaky over the past month and even moreso since Jensen Huang left Nvidia. Not the most confident market headed into the 2nd $1T+ IPO of the year.

Recent findings suggest that so what does it mean for today’s price action? Personally, I expect a pop to the $95-$105 level that Hyperliquid has been pricing out for weeks, and it likely sees a spike higher. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the new (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.

We will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.

  • According to recent reports, silk pillowcases not only do wonders for your skin and hair, but they also make your bedscape feel more luxurious.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the best gifts for the women in your life are probably right under your nose. Consider the unique facets of their personality, their hobbies, and what lights them up. Is it watching countless episodes of Barefoot Contessa, dreaming about an upcoming trip to the Poconos, sampling every kind of Sephora mini, or curating a high-design interior vignette? No matter the answer, a great present should match their energy to ensure they end up with something that reflects their essence and also reveals you’ve been paying attention.

According to recent reports, we’ve compiled a curated list of gift ideas tailored to all sorts of interests to minimize the guesswork for birthdays, Mother’s Day, the holiday-gifting scramble, and every momentous occasion in between. Our picks run the gamut—from home decor gems and high-tech gadgets to skin-care gift sets and culinary staples—but are still selective enough to feel special during the massive unboxing reveal.

According to recent reports, silk pillowcases not only do wonders for your skin and hair, but they also make your bedscape feel more luxurious. Gifting her a set is a guaranteed upgrade to her nighttime routine.

In a recent development, A special pair of champagne flutes to mark special occasions and milestones will become a treasured fixture in her barware collection. This cheerful duo features bubbly glass adornments that will pair perfectly with a bottle of her favorite bubbly.

Receiving any Le Creuset cookware is a win for anyone who feels most at home in the kitchen. This Dutch oven is a treat that will become a staple for home chefs, who can use to make endless roasts, stocks, casseroles, and more. So as long as you’re invited for dinner, it’s a win for you, too.

Sources indicate that author Lydia Davis is best known for very short stories, some of them a single sentence long, but her essays are where the reader can see how her mind works. This first volume gathers five decades of writing on reading, translating, Proust, early tourist photographs, and the city of Arles. Complete the gift by dropping her off at a café, where she can read it while people-watching and underlining passages. Don’t forget to buy her favorite coffee.

No gift guide would be complete without a cozy blanket, and we’re making a bid on this mohair one. The colorblocked number is comfortable enough to drape over her shoulders whether she’s snoozing or curled up with a book.

A tablecloth is a smart gift idea for the singular reason that it’s not something you’d really ever buy for yourself. It’s delightfully multiuse: covering the many drink rings on your walnut table, performing as a park blanket in a pinch, and—most importantly—giving your favorite gal a sense of cohesive calmness as she sets her table.

Recent findings suggest that whether or not she has the dreamy silverware to match, Sabre’s serving set with trendy burgundy handles will feel like a little luxury for plating cheese boards and opening bottles. Elegant and slightly retro, they’re versatile enough to accompany both bold and understated tabletop decorations.

In a recent development, paper napkins are fine for any regular evening, but a hostess deserves a beautiful set of cloth linens. Borgo delle Tovaglie, the Italian linen house Valentina Muggia took over from her mother, makes these in soft-washed pure linen. The red colorway is embroidered with an ivory floral motif that makes even takeout look planned.

“Few things are so favored in my home as this tabletop lighter,” states shopping writer Julia Harrison. “I got it on a whim, and then found myself using it routinely every night.” Perfect for incense, candles, burning cursed love notes, or enjoying a cigarette on the fire escape. Don’t forget the butane.

For the minimalist coffee lover who can’t resist a little chrome, Louise Roe has just the cup-and-saucer set to slide under the tree.

Industry observers note that enza Fasano works in the Apulian pottery tradition of Grottaglie, a town in Puglia, Italy. Her Guido cup and saucer bring the relaxed sense of a Southern Italian breakfast table to an ordinary weekday morning. The jade glaze is a staff favorite, and the set mixes with the line’s other colors if she wants to build a collection. Nota bene: It’s dishwasher-safe.

One thing about many a woman: She loves a pitcher. Not necessarily for pouring lemonade, but for the concept that she could, should the occasion present itself. These thick glass styles from Il Buco Vita double as great vases, too, making them a great hostess gift. They also hold plenty of water for her guests at one of her routine dinner parties.

If getting in a chapter or two of her current book du jour before lights out is a must, she’ll find a new best friend in this little task lamp. The head is magnetized, so you can direct light in pretty much any direction you choose. The sage shade has a notably relaxing quality.

No one has ever been charmed by a cardboard Kleenex box, which is what makes this such a satisfying find. Todd Nickey and Amy Kehoe designed the handmade lacquer tissue box with James Lowther of the Lacquer Manufacturer for a collection drawn from antiques they’ve collected over the years. The cover, made in Vietnam, slips over most standard tissue boxes. In khaki and chocolate, it will look at home on a nightstand or vanity long after cold season ends.

Industry observers note that the year’s best photo deserves better than her camera roll. For the Ornament, Framebridge prints a picture you upload and sets it in a tiny frame on a green velvet ribbon, with a hidden pocket on the back for a note, then ships it in a vintage-style matchbox.
